keyword: what happens if i file taxes late
claims: The failure-to-file penalty is 5% of the unpaid taxes for each month or part of a month that a tax return is late.
The failure-to-file penalty maxes out at 25%.
If a tax return is filed more than 60 days late, the minimum penalty is $525 or 100% of the unpaid tax, whichever is less.
The failure-to-pay penalty is 0.5% of the unpaid taxes for each month or partial month.
The failure-to-pay penalty is capped at 25%.
If both failure-to-file and failure-to-pay penalties apply, the penalties can reach up to 47.5% of the tax owed.
The IRS charges interest on underpayments.
Interest on underpayments accrues from the tax deadline until the date of payment.
There is no penalty for filing late if you are owed a refund.
You must file within three years of the original deadline to claim a refund if you are owed one.
The failure-to-file penalty is ten times higher than the failure-to-pay penalty.
Form 4868 provides an automatic six-month extension to file.
Form 4868 does not extend the time to pay any taxes owed.
